entities.name: α-Hydroxybutyrate
observations: In a cross-sectional study of 217 adults at increased diabetes risk, fasting serum α-HB above 3.9 µg/mL was associated with higher OGTT glucose exposure and a reduced initial insulin-response slope.
Adding α-HB to age, sex, BMI, fasting glucose, HbA1c, and fasting insulin increased AUC for predicting 1-hour glucose ≥155 mg/dL from 0.82 to 0.86; p=0.015; net reclassification index 52%, p<0.0001.

entities.name: PMID:25452875
observations: Varvel et al., BMJ Open Diabetes Research & Care, 2014;2:e000038. Cross-sectional study using 75-g OGTT with serial glucose and insulin measurements in 217 adults at increased diabetes risk; 25% had impaired glucose tolerance.

entities.name: 1-hour glucose ≥155 mg/dL
observations: The study used 1-hour glucose ≥155 mg/dL as the abnormal OGTT endpoint; α-HB improved multivariable discrimination when added to traditional risk factors.

entities.name: Early-phase β-cell dysfunction
observations: Higher α-HB tertiles showed a reduced initial slope of insulin response during OGTT, interpreted by the authors as impaired early insulin secretion kinetics; the abstract does not report a standard insulinogenic-index estimate.
